case_number: Civil Appeal No. 5037 of 2022 (Arising out of S.L.P. (C) No. 24287 of 2018)
summary: The appellants, teachers in state educational institutions, challenged the State of Kerala’s failure to enhance the retirement age to 65 years despite adopting the UGC (Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers) Regulations, 2010 and accepting 80% central financial assistance for pay revision. The central issue was whether the enhancement of superannuation age to 65 was a mandatory condition for receiving central funds. The Supreme Court considered the UGC Act, 1956—particularly Section 20, which gives the Central Government final authority on policy matters relating to national purposes—and the 2010 UGC Regulations, which tied revised pay scales to adherence to central directives. The Court noted a subsequent 2012 MHRD circular de-linking the age enhancement condition from central financial assistance, leaving age of retirement to state discretion. The Court held that the requirement to raise retirement age was no longer binding due to the 2012 amendment, thereby upholding the State of Kerala’s right to decide on retirement age independently.
legal_provisions_cited: Entry 66, Union List, Seventh Schedule, Constitution of India

University Grants Commission (Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges and Other Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Higher Education) Regulations, 2010
P. Suseela & Ors. v. University Grants Commission & Ors., (2015) 8 SCC 129
final_judgment: The appeal was dismissed. The Supreme Court upheld the impugned judgment of the Kerala High Court, affirming that the State of Kerala is not obligated to enhance the retirement age of teachers to 65 years as a condition for receiving central financial assistance, following the 2012 MHRD circular de-linking the requirement.
